title: Final Fantasy's Numbers Were Wrong in America for Years
hook:
The Final Fantasy III that Americans played on the SNES in 1994 was really Final Fantasy VI, and the real II, III and V took up to 16 years to arrive. Which one did you play under the wrong number?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.

script: Did you know Final Fantasy's numbers were wrong in America for most of the nineties? Back in nineteen ninety one, Square released Final Fantasy Four in Japan on the Super Famicom console. When it reached the Super Nintendo in America that November, the box said Final Fantasy Two. That happened because the real Final Fantasy Two and Three never left Japan at the time. Square skipped them and simply renumbered the next game. The American version was also simplified, with some items and battle commands removed. Then Final Fantasy Five came out in Japan in nineteen ninety two, and Square looked hard at bringing it over. Square translator Ted Woolsey later said it was just not accessible enough for the average American player. So that one was skipped too. When Final Fantasy Six arrived in America in nineteen ninety four, the box called it Final Fantasy Three. Final Fantasy Seven on the PlayStation finally lined the numbers back up. The missing games took years to catch up. Five finally arrived inside the Final Fantasy Anthology collection on PlayStation in nineteen ninety nine. Two came along in the Final Fantasy Origins collection on PlayStation in two thousand three. Three waited all the way until the Nintendo DS remake in two thousand six. So did you grow up thinking Kefka was the villain of Final Fantasy Three? Follow for more gaming history.
